Henrik Norbeck’s version

The above transcription is from the Henrik Norbeck collection and differs only in a few notes from the version submitted.
Personally, I prefer Tanya’s version as it is closer to what Paddy O’Brien actually wrote.

Paddy O‘Brien’s daughter, Eileen O’Brien Minogue has produced a book of Paddy’s compositions entitled “The Compositions of Paddy O’Brien” published 1992 by J.D.C Publications Ltd.,
36 Westportland Street, Troon, Ayrshire, Scotland, KA 106AB.

There are many excellent tunes in it. I don’t believe Paddy composed a bad one.

↳ Posted by milesnagopaleen on August 22nd, 2003.

Hanley’s Tweed, X:7

This is the setting I play, with my personal choice with the triplets.

I play it here:

https://youtu.be/iDcIqdO_fVg

I am using two harmonicas, one in C and another in G. I am using the G harmonica to play the pedal note bit at the beginning and a few notes more in order to do the harmonica change in a good place. That pedal note in the C harmonica is quite hard to do as all the notes are on the draw.

Explained with colours here:

https://imgur.com/a/8vPzCx6

Orange => pedal note.
Yellow => extra notes that I play on the G harmonica.

↳ Posted by Fernando Durbán Galnares on January 15th, 2023.
